fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestShipGateRunLog|TestShipRebase' shows: with RHIZA_RUN set, a failing gate whose output is over 64 KB with '--- FAIL: TestX' near its start and make's error lines at its end writes a log in the run's directory holding every byte, the response's log field names it, and the last 20 lines of the human output contain '--- FAIL: TestX' and 'Full log: <path>'; a second gate run in the same run writes a second file and leaves the first intact; a passing gate also writes its log; with no RHIZA_RUN the log is rhiza/gate/<branch>.log under the git common dir; a ship-change gate command step that fails keeps a journal detail naming the log path; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/describe-golden passes after regenerating it for the new field; go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow passes; grep -c 'run `rhiza ship gate` to see' internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml .rhiza/workflows/ship-change.toml prints 0 for both and each gate-fix prompt names the full gate log; make self-check passes
fields.statement: Each local gate run (rhiza ship gate, and the gate ship rebase runs on a merged head) writes its whole combined output to its own log file in the run's directory, never overwriting an earlier gate log of that run (outside a run, rhiza/gate/<branch>.log under the git common dir); ShipGateResponse's log field and the gate step's journal entry carry the path, a failing gate's human output ends with its failing test lines (go test '--- FAIL:', 'FAIL', 'panic:', at most 10) and 'Full log: <path>', and the gate-fix prompts tell the fixer to read that log instead of rerunning the gate
